ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During the ripening process of banana fruit, the stored substances in the fruit are continuously metabolized and transformed, and the banana gradually becomes sweeter. In Figure A, curves I and II respectively indicate the changing trends in the contents of two substances during the ripening process of banana fruit. Please answer:
Take equal amounts of banana pulp ripened to day X and day Y, and add equal amounts of distilled water respectively to make extracts. Then add 5mL of the extract from day X to each of test tubes a and b, and add 5mL of the extract from day Y to each of test tubes c and d, as shown in Figure B. After adding equal amounts of iodine solution to test tubes a and c respectively, tube a turns blue. What is the substance being tested in the two tubes?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of Figure A is a coordinate graph, with the vertical axis as “content of two substances” and the horizontal axis as “ripening time (d)”. As the ripening time advances from X to Y, curve I gradually decreases, and curve II gradually increases. On the right side of Figure B there are four test tubes a, b, c, and d, among which a and b are labeled as the extract from day X, and c and d are labeled as the extract from day Y; above test tubes a and c it is labeled to add “iodine solution”, and above test tubes b and d it is labeled to add “Fehling's reagent”. Reasoning: The stem says that after adding equal amounts of iodine solution to test tubes a and c, tube a turns blue. In biological experiments, iodine solution is used to identify starch, and it turns blue when it encounters starch. Therefore, adding iodine solution to tubes a and c is testing for starch, and tube a turning blue indicates that the extract from day X contains starch. From this it can be known that the substance being tested in these two tubes is starch.
